chapter: Looking back and the New York years
title: Mixed audiences in camps; police harassment in Boise
summary: Army camp theatres were mixed without problems, but police in Boise, Idaho questioned the musicians in town.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Was the Army segregated at that time, or were you playing to White and Black soldiers?
We were playing White and Black. We were always playing one of them theatres... They'd have a theatre in all them Army camps. A theatre.
Yeah. They were all sitting there mixed. The soldiers all sitting out there.
Because I know down South there were one or two rather nasty incidents.
Yeah. I guess that's why maybe they didn't send us South. We never did run into nothin'. Now, ..(?).. when we got into Idaho, the law was kind of bothering us out there.

Well, there'd be a town where we worked at, and we'd be going up there walking around the town or something like that. We just made our tracks scarce up there. You know, sometimes you would walk... We'd be in them Army camps, be way out where you wouldn't see no people, nothin' but the soldiers, and when we'd come to town we might want to buy a new shirt or

some shoes or get some handkerchiefs or some towels, or something like that. And you'd get down there, and the Law would see you there and they'd want to know where you come from and who are you, where you work at and all that kind of stuff.
That's real sort of backwards country.
